questions.q: A supplier in Aba finds that he undercharged a retailer in Port Harcourt by ₦7,000 in an invoice already sent. Which document will he send to correct the undercharge?
questions.explanation: A debit note is sent to correct an undercharge by informing the buyer of an additional amount owed. A credit note is used when the buyer has been overcharged or has returned goods.

questions.q: Adebayo buys 1,500 shares at ₦12.50 per share. His stockbroker charges brokerage of 2% of the cost of the shares. What is the total amount Adebayo pays?
questions.explanation: The cost of the shares is 1,500 × ₦12.50 = ₦18,750. Brokerage is 2% of ₦18,750 = ₦375, so the total paid is ₦18,750 + ₦375 = ₦19,125. Omitting brokerage would wrongly give ₦18,750.

questions.q: A company in Ibadan wishes to raise additional capital by offering new ordinary shares to its existing shareholders in proportion to their present holdings. This offer is known as
questions.explanation: A rights issue offers new shares to existing shareholders in proportion to their holdings, usually to raise fresh capital. A bonus issue gives existing shareholders free shares from reserves and does not raise new capital.

questions.q: A trader in Onitsha deliberately sets fire to his own warehouse in order to collect money from his insurer. This conduct is an example of
questions.explanation: Moral hazard refers to dishonest or careless conduct by an insured person that increases the risk of loss, such as deliberately damaging insured property to claim compensation. Insurable interest is a financial relationship with the subject matter, while utmost good faith requires full disclosure.

questions.q: Yakubu in Ilorin takes a motor insurance policy that covers injury to other persons and damage to their property but does not cover damage to his own car. This cover is
options: third party fire and theft cover
questions.explanation: Third party only cover protects the insured against liability for injury or damage caused to other people and their property. Comprehensive cover also pays for damage to the insured person's own vehicle.

questions.q: A Nigerian manufacturer exporting goods to another ECOWAS member state wants to claim preferential tariff treatment under the ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme. Which document is most important for proving the origin of the goods?
questions.explanation: A certificate of origin shows the country in which the goods were produced and is required to support preferential treatment under an origin-based trade scheme. A bill of lading is mainly a carriage and title document, while a consular invoice and a packing list do not establish the origin of the goods.

questions.q: A firm in Kano studies what buyers dislike about existing brands of footwear before producing its own shoes. This approach best illustrates the
questions.explanation: The marketing concept begins with identifying customer needs and wants and then producing goods to satisfy them. The production and product concepts focus mainly on making goods efficiently or improving the product without first studying buyers, while the selling concept emphasises aggressive selling of what has already been produced.

questions.q: A company in Lagos gives free samples of a new toothpaste at a shopping centre and includes a discount coupon in each pack. These activities are examples of
questions.explanation: Free samples and discount coupons are short-term incentives used to encourage customers to try or buy a product, which is sales promotion. Advertising is a paid non-personal message, personal selling involves direct contact with a salesperson, and publicity is unpaid public attention.

questions.q: A mobile phone seller in Abuja includes a charger, earphones and a one-year warranty with every phone sold. In the marketing mix, these items belong to
questions.explanation: Product covers the goods and all benefits attached to them, including accessories and warranties. Price is the amount charged, promotion covers communication with buyers, and place concerns distribution to customers.

questions.q: The fact that a ₦1,000 note can be exchanged for ten ₦100 notes without loss of value illustrates the quality of money known as
questions.explanation: Divisibility is the ability of money to be broken into smaller units whose total value equals the original amount. Portability concerns ease of carrying money, durability is resistance to wear, and acceptability is willingness of people to receive it as payment.

questions.q: A fashion designer in Abuja sells clothes through her social media page. Customers pay online and choose home delivery. This type of e-commerce is best described as
questions.explanation: The fashion designer's business sells directly to final consumers online, so the transaction is business-to-consumer. Consumer-to-consumer involves individuals selling to one another, business-to-business involves firms trading with firms, and consumer-to-government involves individuals dealing with government agencies.

questions.q: The conversion of timber into chairs and tables by a carpenter creates
questions.explanation: Turning timber into furniture changes the physical form of the material and makes it more useful, which is form utility. Transport creates place utility, storage creates time utility, and buying or selling creates possession utility.

questions.q: A trader in Kano stores bags of onions in a warehouse and releases them during a period of scarcity. The utility created is
questions.explanation: Keeping onions until they are needed at a later period changes their availability over time, so the storage creates time utility. The onions are not changed in form, moved to another place, or transferred in ownership by the mere act of storage.

questions.q: A courier rider in Lagos asks a customer to sign a form after delivering a parcel. The main purpose of the signature is to
options: serve as insurance for the goods in transit
confirm that the parcel has been delivered
authorise customs inspection of the parcel
show that the sender has paid the courier charge
questions.explanation: The signature confirms that the parcel was handed over to the named recipient or their agent, so it is proof of delivery. It does not by itself prove that postage was paid, authorise customs action, or provide insurance cover.

questions.q: A horticultural firm in Jos wants to send freshly cut flowers to a buyer in London. Which mode of transport is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Fresh flowers are highly perishable and need rapid delivery, so air transport is the most suitable. Sea, road and rail would take too long for the flowers to reach London in good condition.

questions.q: In a consumers' cooperative society in Ilorin, surplus is usually shared among members according to
options: the number of meetings each member attended
the age of each member in the society
the value of goods each member bought from the society
the amount of fixed deposit each member holds
questions.explanation: In a consumers' cooperative, surplus is returned to members in proportion to their purchases or patronage. It is not shared according to meeting attendance, fixed deposits or the age of members.

questions.q: One disadvantage of converting a family business into a public limited company is that the business
options: loses the ability to employ salaried managers
can no longer transfer its shares
cannot own property in its own name
must make its accounts available for public inspection
questions.explanation: A public limited company must file and publish annual accounts, exposing its financial affairs to public scrutiny. It can employ managers, own property in its own name, and its shares are generally transferable, so those are not disadvantages.

questions.q: A wholesaler in Aba delivers cartons of beverages to a retailer on the understanding that payment will be made after the retailer has sold the goods. This credit facility offered by the wholesaler is known as
questions.explanation: Trade credit is the credit given by one trader to another for goods supplied, allowing later payment. A cash discount is a reduction for prompt payment, while a quantity discount is a price reduction for buying in large quantities.

questions.q: Mrs. Bello in Kano chooses goods from a catalogue sent by a retail firm and receives them by courier after placing her order by telephone. This type of retailing is
questions.explanation: Mail order retailing involves selling goods through catalogues, with customers ordering by post or telephone and receiving the goods by delivery. Departmental and multiple shop retailing are carried out through physical stores, while street trading involves selling in public places.

questions.q: A customer in Ilesha pays more for a tin of milk at a nearby kiosk than at a supermarket mainly because the kiosk operator
options: charges value added tax while supermarkets are exempted from tax
sells all goods on credit to customers
buys in small quantities and does not enjoy bulk purchase discounts
pays higher salaries to more staff than the supermarket
questions.explanation: A small retailer usually buys stock in small quantities, so the cost per unit is higher than for a supermarket that buys in bulk. The other statements are not general reasons: tax rules do not exempt supermarkets in that way, small kiosks do not normally pay more staff salaries, and selling on credit would tend to raise rather than lower prices.

questions.q: A road transport company in Jos issues a trader with a document that gives details of goods carried and the freight charge, and accompanies the goods to the destination. This document is a
questions.explanation: A consignment note is used for goods sent by road or rail and gives details of the goods and transport charges. A bill of lading performs a similar function for sea carriage, while an invoice shows the selling price of goods.

questions.q: Before a company issues new shares to the public, an institution agrees to buy any shares not taken up by the public. The institution is acting as an
questions.explanation: An underwriter undertakes to buy any shares not taken up by the public, thereby reducing the risk of an unsuccessful issue. A stockbroker buys and sells shares for clients, while a registrar keeps the register of shareholders.

questions.q: A trader's shop in Ibadan was destroyed when a fire from a neighbouring generator set caused an explosion. In deciding whether the fire policy covers the loss, the insurer looks for the immediate or effective cause of the damage. The insurance principle applied is
questions.explanation: Proximate cause is the immediate or effective cause of a loss; the insurer uses it to determine whether the loss falls within the cover. Indemnity concerns restoring the insured financially, while contribution and subrogation concern sharing or recovering claim costs.

questions.q: A Nigerian importer in Kaduna buys machinery from Japan for 12,500 US dollars. If the exchange rate is ₦1,600 to 1 US dollar and the bank charges 2% of the naira value, how much will the importer pay in total?
questions.explanation: The naira value of the goods is 12,500 × ₦1,600 = ₦20,000,000. The bank charge is 2% of ₦20,000,000, which is ₦400,000. The total payment is ₦20,000,000 + ₦400,000 = ₦20,400,000.

questions.q: In a particular year, a country's visible exports were ₦18.5 trillion while its visible imports were ₦12.3 trillion. What was the country's balance of trade?
questions.explanation: The balance of trade is visible exports minus visible imports. Here, ₦18.5 trillion − ₦12.3 trillion = ₦6.2 trillion. Since exports exceeded imports, the balance is a surplus.

questions.q: A detergent company in Lagos changes its sachet from a plain rectangular shape to one with a resealable corner and a handle. This modification is a decision under which element of the marketing mix?
questions.explanation: Packaging, design and physical features are part of the product element of the marketing mix. Price deals with the amount charged, promotion with communication, and place with distribution.

questions.q: A new restaurant in Owerri fixes the price of its lunch pack at ₦2,990 rather than ₦3,000, hoping customers will see it as cheaper. Which pricing strategy is being used?
questions.explanation: Psychological pricing uses non-round figures to create the impression that a product is cheaper than it really is. Penetration pricing involves a low introductory price, while price skimming starts with a high price for a new product.

questions.q: A newly licensed mobile network operator in Jos pays a popular musician to feature in television and social media advertisements that explain its call and data plans. The main promotional purpose of the advertisements is to
options: announce the technical specifications of the company's network equipment
provide existing users with free after-sales repair advice
create awareness of the plans and persuade consumers to subscribe
remind existing subscribers about plans they have used for many years
questions.explanation: The advertisements introduce a new service and attempt to convince consumers to subscribe, which involves creating awareness and persuading buyers. Reminding long-standing users and giving repair advice are not the main purposes of launching a new service through celebrity adverts.

questions.q: Which of the following is recorded on the assets side of a commercial bank's balance sheet?
options: Bank's borrowings from the Central Bank
questions.explanation: Loans and advances are amounts owed to the bank by borrowers, so they are assets of the bank. Fixed deposits, unpaid dividends and borrowings from the Central Bank are obligations or liabilities of the bank.

questions.q: A tailor in Aba displays samples of clothes on a social media page and receives orders from customers in Port Harcourt and Abuja through WhatsApp. The main advantage of this method over operating only a physical shop is that it
options: removes the need to deliver goods to customers
guarantees that every order will be paid for immediately
enables the tailor to reach a wider market at relatively low cost
eliminates the need to keep records of sales
questions.explanation: Online display and messaging allow a small business to reach customers far beyond its physical location without renting additional shops. It does not remove delivery needs, guarantee immediate payment, or make sales record-keeping unnecessary.

questions.q: An online electronics shop in Lagos allows buyers to rate products and read previous customers' comments before placing orders. This feature mainly helps the shop to
options: speed up the delivery of goods to buyers
prevent the shop from keeping inventory
reduce the price of products automatically
build buyer confidence by showing other customers' experiences
questions.explanation: Product ratings and reviews give potential buyers evidence of how earlier customers experienced the goods, which can increase trust. They do not automatically change prices, shorten delivery time, or remove the need to manage stock.

questions.q: A worker in Ogun State who cuts down trees in a forest to obtain timber is engaged in which type of occupation?
questions.explanation: Cutting down trees to obtain timber is an extractive activity because raw materials are taken directly from nature. Manufacturing changes raw materials into finished goods, while constructive occupations build structures and commercial occupations involve trade and distribution.

questions.q: An insurance company in Lagos compensates a trader when fire damages her warehouse. The service provided by the insurance company is best classified as
questions.explanation: Insurance is a commercial service provided to protect persons or businesses against risk, so it is classified as an indirect service. Direct personal services involve close personal attention, while extractive and constructive occupations deal with raw materials and building structures.

questions.q: A company in Kano buys raw hides and skins and turns them into leather shoes for sale. The company is mainly engaged in
questions.explanation: Turning raw hides and skins into leather shoes changes raw materials into manufactured goods, which is secondary production. Primary production involves extraction from nature, and tertiary production involves providing services.

questions.q: In the communication process, the response of a receiver to a message is important mainly because it
options: prevents the use of a communication medium
guarantees that the message is short
shows whether the receiver understood the message
questions.explanation: The response is feedback, and it helps the sender know whether the message has been received and understood as intended. Feedback does not remove the need for a medium or for encoding, nor does it determine the length of the message.

questions.q: A business that is owned and controlled by its members, who share profits according to their patronage and have one vote each, is best described as a
questions.explanation: A cooperative society operates on the principle of one member, one vote and shares surplus according to members' patronage. A public limited company uses shareholding, a partnership is formed by partners, and a public corporation is owned by government.

questions.q: When the debts of a partnership exceed the firm's assets, the partners may be required to pay the balance from their personal property. This shows that the partners have
questions.explanation: In an ordinary partnership, partners have unlimited liability, so personal property can be used to settle business debts beyond the firm's assets. Limited liability, perpetual succession and separate legal personality are features more associated with incorporated companies.

questions.q: A retailer in Kaduna buys a carton of soap from a wholesaler and sells the bars of soap individually to final consumers. The main function the retailer is performing is
questions.explanation: The retailer divides the wholesaler's large consignment into smaller units that consumers can buy. Hoarding means storing goods in the hope of higher prices, while underwriting and cheque clearing are not retail functions.

questions.q: A company operates twenty identical supermarkets in different towns, with central buying, common management and uniform prices. This type of retail organization is known as
questions.explanation: Multiple shops are several similar retail outlets owned and controlled by one firm and run with centralized buying. A departmental store is one large store divided into departments, while a retail cooperative is owned by members.

questions.q: A shoe manufacturer in Aba sells his shoes directly to final consumers without passing through wholesalers or retailers. This channel of distribution is called
questions.explanation: Direct selling occurs when the producer deals with the final consumer without intermediaries. Hire purchase is a payment method, and warehousing is storage rather than a channel of distribution.

questions.q: The part of the Nigerian Exchange where investors buy and sell shares that have already been issued and are currently held by shareholders is called the
questions.explanation: The secondary market deals in existing securities, allowing holders to sell to other investors. The primary market is where a company first issues new shares to raise capital.

questions.q: Shares described as blue chips on the stock exchange are shares of companies that
options: were issued only in the current year and have never been traded
are held exclusively by the government
pay only a fixed rate of interest and must be redeemed at a fixed date
are large, reputable and have a long record of stable earnings
questions.explanation: Blue-chip shares belong to well-established companies with a reputation for stable performance and dividends. Newly issued shares have no such record, and fixed-interest redeemable securities are bonds or debentures rather than ordinary blue-chip shares.

questions.q: A marine insurance policy that covers goods for a particular journey from Lagos to Douala, beginning when the goods leave the named port and ending when they reach their destination, is called
questions.explanation: A voyage policy is arranged for a stated journey, so cover follows the goods from the named origin to destination. A time policy runs for a fixed period, while a valued policy fixes the value of the insured subject matter.

questions.q: Ngozi, an importer in Apapa, Lagos, brings in goods valued at ₦12,000,000. If import duty is charged at 20 per cent of the value of the goods, how much duty does she pay?
questions.explanation: Import duty is 20 per cent of the value: (20 ÷ 100) × ₦12,000,000 = ₦2,400,000. The ₦1,200,000 figure comes from using 10 per cent, while ₦4,800,000 comes from using 40 per cent.

questions.q: A country’s export price index is 150 and its import price index is 120. What is the country’s terms of trade?
questions.explanation: Terms of trade = (export price index ÷ import price index) × 100 = (150 ÷ 120) × 100 = 125. Using the inverse ratio gives 80, and subtracting or averaging the indices gives the other tempting figures.

questions.q: A soap manufacturer in Ilorin gives its washing soap a unique name, symbol and colour combination so that customers can easily identify it among similar products. This practice is an example of
questions.explanation: Branding gives a product a distinctive name, symbol or design that identifies it and distinguishes it from competing products. Labelling gives information on the product, while packaging protects or contains it.

questions.q: A sachet milk producer in Kaduna prints the manufacturer’s address, ingredients, production date and expiry date on the wrapper of each sachet. This information constitutes the product’s
questions.explanation: The printed information such as ingredients, address and expiry date on a product is its label. A brand identifies the producer's product, and a package is the container or wrapper itself.

questions.q: A shoe company in Aba carries out a survey to find out the styles and sizes customers prefer before it starts production. This practice best illustrates the
questions.explanation: The marketing concept begins with identifying customers' needs and then designing products to satisfy them. The production concept stresses availability and low cost, the selling concept stresses aggressive selling, and the product concept stresses product features without first studying customer needs.

questions.q: A bank in Ibadan lends ₦500,000 to a customer who deposits her gold jewellery with the bank as security for repayment. The gold jewellery is best described as
questions.explanation: Collateral is an asset pledged by a borrower as security for a loan, so the bank can sell it if repayment fails. Premium relates to insurance, interest is the charge for borrowing money, and capital is the owner's investment or funds.

questions.q: An online bookshop in Lagos accepts and processes orders at any time of the day or night. This benefit of e-commerce is best described as
questions.explanation: E-commerce allows a business to receive and process orders at any time without the restrictions of shop opening hours, which is round-the-clock trading. Wider market reach concerns distance, lower overhead cost concerns expenses, and improved security is not the benefit described.
